malicious_snippets.code_snippet: PowerShell-based implant code executed within a .NET application, avoiding direct invocation of powershell.exe.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code executes PowerShell commands within a .NET application context, enabling command and control communication and remote code execution, while evading detection by not launching powershell.exe.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Executing PowerShell code without launching powershell.exe is a known evasion technique used by malware to bypass security monitoring.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate .NET applications do not typically embed and execute PowerShell scripts covertly, especially without user interaction or clear administrative purpose.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some legitimate administrative tools may embed PowerShell for automation, but this is usually documented and transparent.
key_indicators: PowerShell code execution within .NET without powershell.exe process

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: RAT code with self-removal capability to erase its presence after initial access.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code provides remote access to the attacker, enables command execution, and can remove itself from the system to cover tracks.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Self-removal after initial access is a strong indicator of anti-forensic behavior, commonly used by malware to evade detection and analysis.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate remote access tools do not typically erase themselves after use, especially without user consent.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some legitimate installers may clean up temporary files, but not full self-removal of remote access components.

attack_chain.action: Initial compromise via spear phishing or vulnerability exploitation.
Deployment and execution of PowerLess Backdoor for command and control.
Deployment of StrifeWater RAT for initial access and remote control.
attack_chain.leads_to: Further lateral movement or data exfiltration

attack_chain.action: Self-removal of RAT to cover tracks and evade detection.

behavioral_signatures: PowerShell code execution within .NET applications without powershell.exe process
Remote access tool with self-removal/anti-forensic capabilities
Unusual network connections from .NET or unknown binaries
file_indicators: Unknown .NET executables with embedded PowerShell scripts
network_indicators: Unusual or encrypted traffic to attacker-controlled domains
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for .NET applications executing PowerShell code without spawning powershell.exe, look for binaries with self-removal or anti-forensic routines, and alert on suspicious outbound network connections from unknown or recently installed executables.
